newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas turns narrowly mixed late, cash firms.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas turns narrowly mixed late, cash firms.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures turned narrowly mixed late Friday in thin activity, but warmer weekend weather forecasts for the Northeast and Midwest helped keep spot-August in positive territory.
At 1420 EDT, August was up 0.3 cent at $2.118 per million British thermal units, while September was 0.1 cent higher at $2.125. Other deferreds were narrowly mixed.

"I'm impressed August hasn't fallen, but cash seems to have a lot more support than futures," said one Texas-based trader, adding near-term weather forecasts and strong power prices offered little incentive to sell aggressively now.

Weekend weather forecasts for the Midwest and Northeast are calling for above-normal temperatures that should last into early next week, but more seasonal weather is expected later in the week. Heat is expected to continue in Texas and the Southwest.

While longer-term, many feel growing storage will weigh on the market, technical traders said they expected August to stay range-bound for now, with support still at this week's low of $2.051 and resistance first at $2.15. Major selling should surface along the down trendline at $2.24, with psychological buying likely at $2.
"If we can get through $2.15 (basis August), we could see some (buy) stops," said a Midwest player.

In the cash Friday, weekend Gulf Coast prices edged up one cent to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also was modestly higher near the $2.40 level.
NYMEX said 11,285 contracts traded at 1350 EDT.
On the KCBT, August was still up one-half cent at $2.01, while deferreds remained steady to three cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed 0.2 cent to 10.8 cents (NYMEX premium).
